claimed.text: To The Stars Academy announced in July 2019 that it had acquired metamaterials it described as originating from an advanced aerospace vehicle of unknown origin. Its executive Steve Justice, a former Skunk Works program director, said their structure and composition are "not from any known existing military or commercial application".

How the ADAM samples reached the company: Linda Moulton Howe says they were tested by Carnegie Science's Department of Terrestrial Magnetism in 1996 and again by Harold Puthoff and others on several occasions. The board's own reconstruction, which no single document sets out, runs from an anonymous source to Art Bell in the 1990s, to Howe, to Carnegie and Puthoff, to To The Stars for $35,000, to the Army agreement, and then goes dark until AARO's acquisition.
Justice himself stated that the materials "have been collected from sources with varying levels of chain-of-custody documentation".

On the board's inference, ADAM's value was custodial and legal rather than scientific: it created a private chain of custody outside the classification system, the only posture under which such material could go to an Army laboratory under an unclassified instrument.
The magnesium specimen sent to Oak Ridge was, according to AARO's records page, publicly alleged to come from a crashed extraterrestrial vehicle of 1947.
Garry Nolan has said that study of small samples of exotic material could yield "hundreds of technology revolutions".

Reporting by NewsNation and Popular Mechanics says ORNL scientists examined the magnesium specimen for technosignatures using scanning transmission electron microscopy after finding no biosignatures, and found no evidence of extraterrestrial origin.

The retired Senate Armed Services staffer Kirk McConnell said on American Alchemy in April 2025 that the contract forming AARO's advisory group under Kirkpatrick was let through Oak Ridge. He does not allege wrongdoing and does not name the group, and no such task order was located.

contested.text: The Oak Ridge finding does not settle the question it arose from: AARO's reports say the specimen's "undocumented chain of custody and conflicting personal accounts" leave its origin unclear, neither AARO nor ORNL could verify its historical origin, and the comparison baseline of failed magnesium alloys is admittedly incomplete.

Puthoff, who had tested the same Howe samples privately, reported in a 2012 letter that testing had not proved alien origin nor produced any anomalous outcome, with one test pending. EarthTech, the company's research partner, has published no results.
The Army did not endorse the claimed origin: its public affairs officer said the Army's interest was in novel materials and that any speculation as to their origin is immaterial.

The Council Bluffs material has been read conventionally from the start: analyses in the weeks after the event found high-carbon steel and slag, and the 2022 study found no anomalous isotopic values. What remains unexplained is the industrial process, not the isotopes.

The IM1 spherule claims were contested in the peer-reviewed literature: Rudraswami, Singh and Pandey re-evaluated the spherules' proposed origin in Chemical Geology in March 2025, Fernando et al. argued the seismic signal used to localise the search was consistent with truck traffic, and Gallardo argued for coal-ash contamination.

AARO's FY2025 report states that no entity has ever captured or exploited UAP-derived materials while noting it is developing procedures for handling such material. The board infers that two laboratory characterisations of voluntarily surrendered specimens cannot bear the weight of that general negative, since the allegation concerns holdings AARO has never inspected and cannot compel.

Kirkpatrick's move to the laboratory that analysed AARO's specimens has drawn a post-employment question that has been raised publicly and never adjudicated. The board records the January 2026 aluminium analysis appearing while he was there for proximity, not impropriety.

The board's own items disagree about the ADAM chain: one reconstruction has it going dark at the 2019 Army agreement, another follows the specimen through the Army to AARO and Oak Ridge on AARO's own wording and calls it fully documented, and AARO itself calls the specimen's chain of custody undocumented.

lead.text: Physical material is where the argument could be settled by measurement rather than testimony. The board holds three lines of analysis: a peer-reviewed study of the 1977 Council Bluffs molten mass, the To The Stars ADAM samples that passed into an Army research agreement, and AARO's Oak Ridge analyses of a magnesium and an aluminium specimen, both of which came back as terrestrial or conventional alloys.

record.text: Nolan, Vallee, Jiang and Lemke published an instrumental analysis of the Council Bluffs material in Progress in Aerospace Sciences 128 (2022), article 100788. The Nolan laboratory at Stanford applied SIMS and MIBI to the samples at 200 nanometre lateral resolution and five-nanometre depth increments.

The analysis found no anomalous isotopic values but incomplete mixing of the metals in the once-molten mass, indicating an industrial process of unknown origin. Meteorite, satellite or spacecraft debris, aircraft debris, dumped molten metal and thermite were each examined and ruled out on physical grounds.

At Council Bluffs on the evening of 17 December 1977, five independent groups of witnesses saw a red luminous mass descend near a park; the assistant fire chief described a mass of molten metal about four by six feet, and police photographed the scene. Analyses in the weeks after found high-carbon steel and slag. Vallee supplied both the material and the documentary case record for the 2022 study.

AARO contracted Oak Ridge National Laboratory in 2022 to test a magnesium alloy specimen it had acquired, with stakeholder permission, from a private UAP organisation and the US Army. ORNL assessed the specimen as terrestrial in origin and as not meeting the theoretical requirements to function as a terahertz waveguide.
AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I determined that an alleged extraterrestrial spacecraft sample was a manufactured terrestrial alloy of magnesium, zinc and bismuth with trace elements.

AARO's January 2026 Aluminum Materials Analysis Supplement reports an ORNL analysis of a specimen recovered near Flint Ridge State Park, Ohio, whose composition matched Aluminum Association reference alloys 369.1 and A413.1, with no radioactive emissions.

To The Stars Academy's SEC filings describe the ADAM Research Project as acquiring and analysing material samples from advanced aerospace vehicles of unknown origin, in partnership with EarthTech International from August 2018, and record the company paying $35,000 for items including six pieces of bismuth/magnesium-zinc metal and a piece of aluminium.

CRADA 19-15 between To The Stars Academy and the Army's Ground Vehicle Systems Center was signed on 10 October 2019 at Detroit Arsenal by Jeffery Langhout for the Army and Kari DeLonge for the company, with Dr. Joseph Cannon among the government principal investigators and Luis Elizondo as the company's. Its research areas include inertial mass reduction, metamaterials and electromagnetic metamaterial waveguides.

The board's custody record joins the two lines: the privately held specimen passed from the company through the Army to AARO and then to ORNL. AARO confirms the organisation negotiated an agreement in 2019 with the Army to analyse the samples.

On 21 February 2020 the Army's CCDC FOIA officer denied in full twenty-nine emails, one hundred pages, of TTSA-Army correspondence under exemptions (b)(4) and (b)(5); GVSC had released the agreement text within a day of the announcement.

Oak Ridge is a DOE laboratory administered by UT-Battelle, the partnership through which Battelle co-operates it. Sean Kirkpatrick, AARO's first director, left AARO on 1 December 2023 and became Chief Technology Officer for Defense and Intelligence Programs at ORNL.

From the Galileo Project's IM1 expedition, Loeb and colleagues published the recovery and classification of spherules in Research Notes of the AAS in January 2024 and a chemical classification in Chemical Geology in December 2024; Hyung, Cherston, Jacobsen and Loeb followed in March 2025 on the morphology and chemistry of D-type spherules.
The Sol Foundation's Briefing No. 3 of April 2026 is the board's main public exposition of the 2022 paper, setting out the witness record, the 1978 identification, the method and each elimination.

summary.text: The board treats isotope ratio measurement as the discriminating test: the Nolan-Vallee methodology paper specifies it, and the chemistry domain is where that test is run.

On the board's reading, only one alleged UAP sample has a complete public chain of custody from incident through analysis to peer-reviewed publication, the 1977 Council Bluffs mass; every other significant chain ends in a private laboratory, a corporate holding or an unpublished federal agreement. This is the board's inference, not a finding of any document, and the board's own custody record for the ADAM line runs further (see below).

AARO's published physical-specimen work consists of Volume I's magnesium-zinc-bismuth finding and two Oak Ridge National Laboratory analyses, one of a magnesium specimen in April 2024 and one of an aluminium specimen with an AARO supplement dated January 2026.

The board reads the Galileo Project's 2023 Pacific expedition to the IM1 bolide site as a control case, in which claim, rebuttal and re-analysis all appeared in the peer-reviewed literature within eighteen months; this is stated as the board's inference.

The AAWSAP reference documents released by DIA include a materials strand: programmable matter, invisibility cloaking, superconductors in gravity research and ultracapacitors, the last described as having immediate conventional military application and no anomalous content.
